implementation_notes: The .NET base class library ships the interceptor mechanism: DispatchProxy.Create<T, TProxy>() generates a proxy implementing the interface T whose Invoke(MethodInfo, object[]) runs the audit logic and then dispatches to the target - the classic Interceptor + InvocationContext structure becomes a DispatchProxy subclass plus a dependency-injected sink, with MethodInfo and the argument array as the invocation context. Works for any interface and any hosting model, but pays one reflective dispatch per call and cannot proxy classes.
pitfalls: DispatchProxy.Create only proxies interfaces and every call is dispatched reflectively: create the proxy once at composition time, never per call.
Target exceptions surface inside Invoke wrapped in TargetInvocationException - rethrow InnerException or the caller sees a different exception contract.
A sink built on ILogger can be filtered or sampled by log level and dropped during shutdown; security audit records need a destination that is never sampled or discarded.

variants.name: ASP.NET Core action filter / middleware
variants.idiom_name: IAsyncActionFilter or middleware in the ASP.NET Core pipeline
variants.implementation_notes: In an ASP.NET Core application the interceptor is a filter: IAsyncActionFilter.OnActionExecutionAsync gets the ActionExecutingContext and an ActionExecutionDelegate whose await is the proceed() hand-off, so the audit event can be recorded before the action and completed with the outcome afterwards. Prefer this declarative form in web pipelines - it is bound per controller/action or globally and needs no proxy generation - but note that it only covers requests that reach MVC, and not internal service-to-service calls.
pitfalls: Filters only see requests that reach the MVC pipeline: middleware, minimal-API endpoints and internal service calls are separate seams and must be audited explicitly.
A filter that does not await (or does not call) the execution delegate silently short-circuits the action - the audit hook then changes behaviour instead of observing it.
